title: cclog canonical observation v0
description: Canonical observation as stored in the local ledger. CloudEvents 1.0 compatible envelope + cclog extension attributes. Content is never inlined; observations reference content only via content_ref.

id.description: observation_id, UUIDv7. Approximates emit order; not a truth of wall time.

source.description: Opaque device + adapter identity only. Never a username, absolute path, or global machine id.

type.description: dev.cclog.<domain>.<event>.v<n>. Vendor event names are never exposed here.

subject.description: Opaque hierarchical ref path (session/turn/tool...). Opaque tokens only.

time.description: occurred_at: source wall clock of the event.

traceparent.description: W3C trace context, kept as local correlation evidence only. Never re-exported to a destination as-is.

cclogsourceversion.description: Adapter-facing source contract fingerprint, e.g. codex-hook/1.

cclogsourcerecordref.description: Local opaque reference to the raw source record (e.g. a transcript_path locator). Never the bytes or a global path.

cclogobservedat.description: observed_at: when the collector received the event (daemon clock).

cclogpurposehint.description: Nullable inference. Never a fact of capture or an authorization input.

cclogprofile.description: Local routing zone. Anything unclassified defaults to personal. Local-only; not exported to any destination as-is.

cclogcorrelationcluster.description: Optional ingest-time cluster hint when an explicit trace or same-batch evidence identifies the same action. Current semantic correlation, including late arrivals, lives in versioned edges/projections.

content_ref.description: Null in metadata-only mode (the default). Points into the encrypted local vault only when content capture is opted in.

count_bucket.description: Coarse magnitude bucket. Exact counts of sensitive quantities are not stored on T1 rows. Every field of this type is OPTIONAL, and absence is how a producer says NOT MEASURED: `"0"` is a measurement (the source reported a count that fell in the zero bucket), so a producer whose source carries no count must omit the field rather than emit `"0"`. There is deliberately no `null`/`unknown` member here -- a bucket value always means something was counted.

agent_ref.description: Opaque pseudonym of the subagent that produced this observation. Present only when the source said a subagent was responsible -- the Claude Code hook channel carries `agent_id` only inside a subagent. ABSENCE IS NOT `false`: it means the source named no subagent, which under that channel's documented contract is the main loop, but no producer asserts that here.

agent_type.description: The subagent's own name, as the source spells it (e.g. `Explore`, or a plugin-scoped `my-plugin:reviewer`). Vendor-controlled text, so it is held to the same discipline as an integrity marker's `detail`: a plain identifier, or the field is omitted. Never a path, a sentence, or anything a user typed as content.

duration_ms.description: Elapsed milliseconds, measured. `null` means NOT MEASURED -- the producer could not close the interval (e.g. a historical tool result whose starting record is not in the same snapshot). It never means zero. `0` is a real measurement of something that completed within a millisecond, so a producer that lacks a measurement must emit `null` rather than `0`: the two channels feeding this field (live hooks, historical import) are aggregated together, and a fabricated `0` is indistinguishable from a measurement and biases every aggregate downward.

detail.description: A short, validated label for what was lost (e.g. the record kind, or the name of a missing field). Never source content: producers must reject anything that is not a plain identifier rather than truncate or escape it. `null` when no safe label is available -- the marker's identity is already carried by its subject and dedupe key.

time_basis.description: Which clock this observation's `time` came from. `occurred_at`: the source record's own timestamp, i.e. when the activity happened. `acquired_at`: the time the snapshot holding it was collected -- a fallback used when the record carries no timestamp of its own, and NOT a measurement of when the activity happened. `copied_at`: the source record's own timestamp, on a record that was COPIED out of another transcript and re-stamped when the copy was written -- so it is when the copying happened, not the activity, and the original time is not recoverable from that file. `received_at`: a receipt stamp taken by cclog's own receiver at the moment the source invoked it SYNCHRONOUSLY -- used by the Claude Code hook channel, where the reference states no hook event carries a timestamp of its own, so the receiver's clock is the only time source there is. Absent means the producer took the source record's own timestamp and had nothing to qualify. A consumer putting an observation on a clock must admit absence, `occurred_at` and `received_at`, and must exclude `acquired_at` and `copied_at`. The line is between a measurement of the event's instant and something else standing in for one: `received_at` differs from the event by the time the source took to spawn the receiver, which is milliseconds and bounded, whereas `acquired_at` can be days later and `copied_at` is a different event's time entirely.
